P/anticipatory-application -- Kim et al.'s null correlation between the 1-9 self-report boredom score and any extracted EEG/gaze feature, despite both physiological channels independently indicating boredom in nearly all participants, cautions Part III against assuming convergence between subjective and physiological/behavioral boredom indices even when both separately register the same underlying state.

P/anticipatory-application -- Kim et al.'s operationalization of attentional disengagement as gaze deviation from a defined Area of Interest plus EEG amplitude instability offers Part III a concrete, non-self-report template for what 'losing attention' could mean operationally, useful for interpreting any VLE attention/engagement measure that is not purely self-reported.

P/anticipatory-application -- Kim et al.'s operationalization of monotony directly as the boredom-induction stimulus (deliberately genre-neutral, content-independent) offers Part III a precedent for isolating monotony as distinct from meaninglessness/low-value appraisals; Part III might ask whether its own 'boring' VLE segments conflate repetitive form (monotony) with perceived value (meaninglessness).
